newsitem.title: USA: Danger of faster inflation drawing closer--Volcker.
newsitem.headline: Danger of faster inflation drawing closer--Volcker.

text.p: Former Federal Reserve Chairman Paul Volcker said on Wednesday that the danger of faster inflation was drawing closer and stressed the need to keep prices down for the long-term good of the economy.
"Some of the preconditions (for inflation) are there," he said, pointing in particular to tight labor markets. But he added, "I'm not saying we're in a crisis."

Interviewed on CNBC television, Volcker said that the buoyant stock market was not "inherently dangerous" for the economy. But he voiced concern that many of the younger traders and investors in the market might not realize that its recent extraordinary returns cannot be sustained forever.
Volcker said it was "hard to find fault" with the Federal Reserve given the "very favorable" performance of the economy.
He said though that he was discourged by the amount of criticism that the central bank has endured for its small increase in interest rates in March.
"We want to keep this process going in a very favorable way," Volcker said. "And that means taking precautionary ... moves so that inflation doesn't get out of hand."
